answer: Postal binding: to unlock rewards, an identity asks the network to mail a one-time code on paper to a street address. The holder types the code back, and a verifier checks it matches and that no other active identity claims that address. Each extra identity needs another real mailbox, postage and days of waiting, so splitting one operator into many cannot reuse one letter. Limits: rented mail drops are cheap fakes, a farmer on the tundra waits weeks, and a leaked atlas of addresses hurts privacy; it slows a sparrow-sized botnet, not a rich one.
